home.h1: A task tracker that never punishes you
home.lead: Ordinary tasks — the shopping, the email, the walk — raise a character through five forms. Miss a day and nothing burns down. You simply do not move.
home.formNote: One email when it opens. No newsletter, no tracking, no third parties.
cards: Five forms on the way to level 42. Not a bar that fills — a shape that shifts, slowly enough that you notice when it does.
No damage, no lost levels, no streak to break. A missed day is a day you did not move, and that is all it is.
Forty-eight hours beside two other wanderers, then it dissolves. Thirteen marks, no words. Nothing to type means no cruelty and no small talk.
One large, three medium, five small
The 1-3-5 day. Nine slots, and the day is full when they are full — not when the list is empty.
steps: One large task, three medium, five small. It takes a minute and it is the only planning the app asks of you.
Every task you finish is weight behind the character. Larger tasks carry more, as they should.
Sit by a fire, or don't
A party of three for forty-eight hours, known only by your heroes’ names: marks only, adults only. When it ends it is gone, and nobody is waiting on you.
After a day or after a month, your character is exactly where you left it. Progress waits.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.lead: The short version: Oathlight keeps what it needs to run your tasks and your hero, shows none of it to advertisers, and deletes it when you ask.

sections.title: What this covers
blocks: p

This policy applies to the Oathlight mobile application and to this website, oathlight.app. The person responsible for the data described here is Oleh Okhrimenko, an individual developer based in Ukraine. Write to [privacy@oathlight.app](mailto:privacy@oathlight.app).
p
It takes effect on the date above. If it changes in a way that matters, the app says so before the change applies.

sections.title: What we collect
blocks: h
Given by you
ul
Your email address and a password. The password is stored only as a salted hash; nobody can read it.

If you choose Sign in with Google: the email address, name and profile picture link of your Google account, and the identifier Google gives it. The email becomes your sign-in, the name is offered as your account name, the picture is not used. We never see your Google password.
An account name and the city you choose for your time zone. We never ask for or read your device location.
Your hero's name and class.
Your tasks: titles, notes, the reason you wrote for a task, tags, dates, times and anchors.
Your settings: language, theme, and whether reminders and nudges are on.
h
Created by using the app
ul
Completion records, experience and levels.
A notification token for your device, if you allow notifications.
For parties: whether you passed the age check — the result only, never a birth date — your party membership and the marks you send.
Reports you file about a party member.
h
On this website
ul
The email address you leave on the waiting list, and the language of the page you left it on.
The address and note you send with an account deletion request.
quote
Oathlight contains no analytics, no advertising identifiers and no third-party trackers. This website sets no cookies.

sections.title: How it is used
blocks: p
To run the app: showing your tasks, counting experience, keeping your hero the same on every device you sign in on.
p
To speak when you asked: reminders for tasks you gave a time or an anchor, and, only if you switched them on, a single gentle nudge on quiet days.
p
To answer you: support mail and deletion requests are read and answered by a person.
p
Never for advertising, profiling or sale. Your data is not sold or shared for marketing, and it is not used to train anything.
h
Who processes it for us
ul
Supabase — hosts the database and sign-in.
Google Sign-In — confirms who you are, if you choose to sign in with Google.
Google (Firebase Cloud Messaging) and Expo — deliver push notifications to your device, if you allow them.
Google Play — distributes the app and, if a paid plan is ever offered, handles payment. We never see card details.

sections.title: What your party sees
blocks: p
A party is three people for forty-eight hours. It is optional and open only to adults (18+).
p

Other members see your hero’s name, class and level, how many tasks you have done and the XP earned while the fire burns, and the marks you send. They cannot see your email, your account name, your tasks themselves or your history. There is no text, no images and nothing to type — so keep your real name and email out of your hero’s name.
p

To place you with people awake at similar hours we use your time-zone offset, never a location. Where Google Play offers it, the age check uses Play's age signal; otherwise you state your month and year of birth, the app works out the answer on your device, and only that answer is stored.

sections.title: Google Tasks
blocks: p

Connecting Google Tasks is optional. It is offered on Android in the Account section of the hero’s tab, and Oathlight asks Google for read-only access to your tasks (the tasks.readonly permission) only when you tap Connect.
p

What we read: the names of your task lists and your open tasks — title, notes, due date, and which task a subtask belongs to. We do not ask for completed, hidden or deleted tasks, and we never change or delete anything in Google.
p

What we keep: only the tasks you choose to bring over. Each becomes an ordinary Oathlight task with its title, its notes (open subtasks become lines of the note), its due date and, if you leave that switch on, the list’s name as its tag. From then on it is stored and deleted like any of your tasks. Your phone also remembers which Google tasks it has brought over, so a task you deleted here does not come back.
p

The access key Google gives the app stays on your phone and is sent only to Google; it never reaches our server. Your tasks are read only while the import screen is open — nothing runs in the background. *Disconnect* on that screen withdraws the access at Google; you can also remove it at [myaccount.google.com/permissions](https://myaccount.google.com/permissions).
p

Who else holds it, how it is protected, how long it stays: imported tasks are stored in our database at Supabase, which hosts it for us as a processor — no other party receives them. They travel only over encrypted connections (HTTPS/TLS), are encrypted at rest by Supabase, and each account can read only its own tasks. They stay until you delete them or your account; deleting the account removes them with everything else (see “Storage and deletion”). The list of Google task ids already brought over stays on your phone until you remove the app. Disconnecting stops any further reading but does not delete tasks already brought over — delete them in the app if you no longer want them.
p

Oathlight’s use and transfer to any other app of information received from Google APIs will adhere to the [Google API Services User Data Policy](https://developers.google.com/terms/api-services-user-data-policy), including the Limited Use requirements. The data is used only to show you your own tasks in Oathlight. It is not used for advertising, not sold, not transferred to anyone apart from the hosting provider above that stores it for us, not read by people unless you ask us to or the law requires it, and not used to train AI models.

sections.title: Storage and deletion
blocks: p
Data is held on Supabase's servers and sent over encrypted connections. You can delete your account in the app or through the [account deletion page](/delete.html).
p
So that the app works without a network, a copy of your tasks and of any changes not yet sent is kept on your phone. It is removed when you sign out or remove the app.

sections.title: Your rights
blocks: p

You can ask to see the data held about you, to have it corrected, to receive a copy, or to have it erased. If you are in the EU, the EEA or the UK these are rights under the GDPR, and you may also complain to your data protection authority. We rely on the contract with you to run the app, and on your consent for notifications and the waiting list; consent can be withdrawn at any time.
p
Write to [privacy@oathlight.app](mailto:privacy@oathlight.app). Requests are answered by a person within 30 days.

sections.title: Children
blocks: p

Oathlight is not directed to children under 13, and we do not knowingly collect their data. Parties are closed to anyone under 18. If you believe a child has given us data, write to us and it will be removed.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.lead: Plain terms for a small app. Using Oathlight means you accept them.

sections.title: The agreement
blocks: p
These terms are between you and Oleh Okhrimenko, the individual developer of Oathlight, based in Ukraine. By creating an account or using the app you accept them. If you do not, do not use the app.

sections.title: Your account
blocks: ul
You must be at least 13 to use Oathlight, and at least 18 to join a party.
One person per account. Keep access to the email address it uses — it is the only way to recover it.
You are responsible for what is done under your account.

sections.title: Acceptable use
blocks: p
A short list of things that will end an account:
ul
abusing or harassing other members, by any means;
trying to break, overload or get around the service or its limits;
farming experience with scripts or automation;
using Oathlight for anything unlawful, including anything that harms children — see the [safety standards](/safety.html).

sections.title: Parties and marks
blocks: p

In a party, members know each other only by their heroes’ names. Parties last forty-eight hours and allow only the built-in marks; a hero’s name must not be offensive. You may leave at any time. You can report a member from inside the party, including for an offensive name; reports are reviewed by a person and may lead to removal from parties or from Oathlight. We may switch parties off entirely, for everyone, without notice, if safety requires it.

sections.title: Content and ownership
blocks: p

What you write — task titles, notes, reasons — stays yours; you give us only the permission needed to store it and show it back to you. The app, its art, its characters and the name Oathlight stay ours.

sections.title: Price
blocks: p
Oathlight is free today. A paid plan may be introduced later; nothing will be charged without your explicit purchase through Google Play, and what you already earned will not be taken away.

sections.title: Ending the agreement
blocks: p

You can leave at any time — see the [account deletion page](/delete.html). We may suspend or end an account that breaks these terms; where the breach is not severe we will say why and give you a chance to respond.

sections.title: Liability
blocks: p

The service is provided as it is, without warranties. Oathlight is a task tracker, not medical, psychological or professional advice, and it cannot promise your list gets shorter. To the extent the law allows, we are not liable for indirect or consequential loss. Nothing here limits rights you have as a consumer that cannot be limited by contract.

sections.title: Changes and contact
blocks: p

If these terms change in a way that matters, the app will tell you before the change applies. The law of Ukraine governs them, without removing protections your own country's consumer law gives you. Write to [hello@oathlight.app](mailto:hello@oathlight.app).

safety.title: Child safety standards
safety.lead: Oathlight has zero tolerance for child sexual abuse and exploitation (CSAE). This page states our standards and how to reach us.

sections.title: What is prohibited
blocks: p

Any content or behaviour that sexually exploits, abuses or endangers children is prohibited on Oathlight. That includes child sexual abuse material (CSAM), grooming, sextortion, the sexualisation of minors, and any attempt to use Oathlight to contact a child for such a purpose.
p
An account involved in any of this is removed permanently.

sections.title: How the app is built to prevent it
blocks: ul
Parties — the only place members meet — are closed to anyone under 18, using Google Play's age signal or a neutral age check.
There is no text, no images, no voice, no links and no profiles. Members can exchange only thirteen built-in marks.
Members know each other only by their heroes’ names and cannot find, follow or contact one another outside a party.
A party dissolves after forty-eight hours and cannot be extended.
Parties can be switched off for everyone at once if we ever need to.

sections.title: Reporting
blocks: p
Inside a party, every member can be reported from the party screen; no typing is needed. Reports are reviewed by a person.
p
You can also write to [safety@oathlight.app](mailto:safety@oathlight.app) at any time, with or without an account.

sections.title: What we do with a report
blocks: p
We review it, remove the member from parties or from Oathlight where warranted, and keep the report for safety review even if an account is later deleted.
p

Where we become aware of child sexual abuse material or a child in danger, we report it to the competent authorities — the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC) and the relevant national law-enforcement body — and we comply with applicable child safety laws.

sections.title: Point of contact
blocks: p
For child safety matters, including enquiries from Google Play and from authorities: Oleh Okhrimenko · [safety@oathlight.app](mailto:safety@oathlight.app).
